newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian bank shares rise in speculative trade.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian bank shares rise in speculative trade.

text.p: Speculation surrounding Nigerian bank shares drove them higher on Thursday, dealers said.
The all-share index closed 8422.76 from 8420.78 on Tuesday. The market was closed on Wednesday for a Moslem festival.
"Traders are speculating on banking shares because of the likelihood of many coming to the market to raise capital," one dealer said.
Banks are required by the authorities to shore their capital base nine-fold to a minimum of 500 million naira.
Leading the upsurge was United Bank for Africa which rose 10 kobo to 12.90 naira.
"There is speculation of improved profits and a bonus issue by UBA," one trader said. UBA's annual result is expected soon.
Wema Bank rose by five kobo to 4.00 naira while NAL Merchant Bank gained four kobo to 8.60 naira.
Inland Bank and International Merchant Bank rose two kobo apiece to 1.52 naira and 1.59 naira, respectively while brewer Guinness rose 10 kobo to 7.55 naira.
Food shares were down on persistent selling.
Cadbury ended at 35.30 naira, down five kobo while Nigerian Bottling Company shed 20 kobo at 52.40 naira. Oil marketer Total slid five kobo to 57.60 naira.
